findings.summary: Despite its name, load_items_or_fail hides backend failures by discarding stderr and returning an empty list with exit 0, so a storage error looks like 'no items' and can lead to data loss if the result is written back.
The counter file's contents go into bash arithmetic without a numeric check, so corrupt content quietly resets the counter to 1 and crafted content (e.g. a[$(cmd)]) would run a command.
